title: Post-Selection Probability and Fidelity of Bidirectional Teleportation
authors: Ning Sun, Lei Feng, Pengfei Zhang
abstract: Understanding the scrambling of quantum information is central to many areas of quantum physics, including quantum thermalization, entanglement growth, and quantum information processing. Insights from these studies have, in turn, inspired the development of novel quantum protocols and algorithms. Recently, a bidirectional teleportation protocol was proposed to implement a digital SWAP operation between qubits by leveraging chaotic Hamiltonian evolution combined with measurement and post-selection. In this work, we provide a comprehensive study of two central quantities that characterize the protocol, the post-selection probability and the fidelity, taking into account possible errors in time-reversed dynamics. We show that these quantities can be expressed in terms of standard diagnostics in quantum dynamics, including the Loschmidt echo and its subsystem variant. The results unveil (1) the initial-state dependence of the fidelity and (2) the stability of the post-selection probability in integrable models. Our findings offer practical guidance for the implementation of the protocol on realistic quantum devices.
summary: This paper analyzes a bidirectional teleportation protocol by relating its success metrics—post-selection probability and fidelity—to established measures of quantum dynamics, such as the Loschmidt echo. The key finding is that integrable Hamiltonians provide superior stability against errors in time-reversed evolution compared to chaotic systems. This offers practical guidance for implementing quantum protocols on realistic hardware.
main_problem: The study characterizes the performance of a bidirectional quantum teleportation protocol designed to perform a digital SWAP operation, focusing on how errors in time-reversed dynamics affect key metrics.
main_result: The post-selection probability and fidelity can be related directly to standard quantum dynamics diagnostics like the subsystem Loschmidt echo. Crucially, integrable models are shown to maintain higher performance (larger post-selection probability) compared to chaotic ones when errors are present.
method: Theoretical derivation establishing relationships between protocol metrics ($p(t), F(t)$) and dynamical measures ($	ext{L}_B(t), 	ext{L}(t)$). Numerical simulations were used on the quantum Ising model to validate these theoretical connections.
model_or_system: The system involves a bidirectional teleportation protocol acting on three subsystems (A, B, C) using chaotic Hamiltonian evolution. The analysis is tested using the Quantum Ising model Hamiltonian, which can be tuned between integrable and chaotic regimes.
key_observables: Post-selection probability ($p(t)$), Fidelity ($F(t)$), Loschmidt Echo ($	ext{L}(t)$), Subsystem Loschmidt Echo ($	ext{L}_B(t)$).
important_parameters: Time evolution $t$, error strength $\epsilon$, and the Hamiltonian parameters (e.g., coupling constants $J, g, h$) determining integrability vs. chaos.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on relating protocol performance to established quantum dynamics diagnostics; specific results are derived for both errorless and noisy time-reversed dynamics.
figures_summary: Figure 1 schematically illustrates the teleportation protocol. Figure 2 diagrammatically proves the relationships between $p(t)$, $	ext{L}_B(t)$, and $F(t)$ versus $	ext{L}(t)$. Figure 3 shows numerical results for the errorless Ising model, comparing initial states. Figure 4 compares performance with errors ($\epsilon=0.05$) for integrable vs. chaotic dynamics.
paper_structure: The paper first introduces the bidirectional teleportation protocol and defines the key quantities ($p(t), F(t)$). It then derives theoretical relationships connecting these quantities to Loschmidt echoes. The analysis is applied to the Ising model, comparing errorless (chaotic vs. integrable) and noisy scenarios to draw conclusions about practical implementation.
why_interesting: This work bridges quantum information processing protocols with fundamental concepts of quantum chaos and thermalization diagnostics (Loschmidt echo). Showing that integrability enhances robustness against time-reversal errors is highly relevant for designing fault-tolerant quantum devices.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. The schematic illustration of the bidirectional tele- portation protocol between systems A and C, with reference qubits RA and RC. Here, we allow for errors between the forward and backward evolution Hamiltonians, denoted as H and H′, respectively. It has been established that, un- der scrambled evolution with perfectly reversed dynamics, the protocol provides a probabilistic realization of the SWAP op- eration between A and C systems. The two central quantities governing the protocol are the post-selection probability p(t) and the fidelity of the resulting quantum state F(t).

FIG. 2. The diagrammatic proof of the main relations: (1) between the probability and the subsystem echo, p(t) = LB(t), and (2) between the fidelity and the Loschmidt echo, F(t)p(t) = 2−2NL(t). Here, the overall factor arises from the normalization of the EPR state, which is omitted in the diagrammatic representation. For conciseness, we introduce unitary evolutions U = e−iHABt and V = e−iH′ ABt, and rep- resent the qubits in B by a single thick solid line. The red slash indicates periodic boundary conditions.

FIG. 3. We present the numerical results for the quantum Ising model in the absence of errors in the backward evolution. We fix N = 1, M = 8, and g/J = 1.05, and consider (a) h = 0.5 (chaotic [11, 18]) and (b) h = 0 (integrable). We present the post-selection probability and the fidelity as functions of time t for both ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic initial states, denoted as FM and AFM, respectively. The dashed lines represent the theoretical prediction p(t) = e−sth/2, as described in the main text.

FIG. 4. We present the numerical results for the quantum Ising model with an error ϵ = 0.05. We fix N = 1, M = 8, and g/J = 1.05, and consider the antiferromagnetic initial state. The solid lines correspond to the integrable case with h = 0, while the dashed lines represent the chaotic case with h = 0.5.
